title: Cold rebuild: Invert the dependency
summary: Rebuild Invert the dependency from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Invert the dependency** in *Dependency Inversion*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.title: Rebuild Invert the dependency cold
prompt: `Notifier` creates its own `SmtpSender`, so it cannot be tested. Refactor:
- `interface IMessageSender { void Send(string to, string text); }`
- `Notifier` receives an `IMessageSender` through its constructor and uses it; `Notify(string user)` sends `Hi <user>` to `<user>@example.com`
The tests pass a fake sender that records messages.
**From memory this time.** In the lesson you started from broken code and repaired it. Now the editor is empty:
write the correct version yourself. The tests are the same ones you passed.
